reconcile.note: Fausset reads Ecclesiastes' call to follow your heart as ironic warning rather than command, so it never licenses the self-trusting heart Numbers and Proverbs condemn.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Krüger reads Ecclesiastes 11:9 as a provocative allusion to Numbers 15:39 that deliberately inverts and contradicts the older command.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Thomas Krüger (2004), Qoheleth: A Commentary, Hermeneia (2004).

sides.snippet: …that you not follow after your own heart and your own eyes, after which you use to play the prostitute;
sides.verseText: and it shall be to you for a fringe, that you may look on it, and remember all the commandments of Yahweh, and do them; and that you not follow after your own heart and your own eyes, after which you use to play the prostitute;

sides.snippet: …And walk in the ways of your heart, And in the sight of your eyes…
sides.verseText: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, And let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, And walk in the ways of your heart, And in the sight of your eyes; But know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
